subject.title: sandbox: keep workspaceAccess none workspaces writable

question: Should OpenClaw approve making the isolated `workspaceAccess: "none"` sandbox workspace writable across local Docker/browser and remote/OpenShell filesystem paths while keeping the real agent workspace unmounted?
rationale: The source-level regression is clear, but the fix changes sandbox filesystem write semantics and must be consistent across backend mount tables, filesystem bridges, memory flush behavior, protected skill roots, and docs.

options.title: Approve isolated writable none
options.body: Implement the cross-backend fix so only the sandbox-owned workspace is writable for `none`, with live sandbox proof and regression coverage.

options.title: Keep fail-closed none
options.body: Leave `none` read-only and update docs/tool exposure to make the current restriction explicit.

options.title: Define sandbox write policy first
options.body: Hold this issue until maintainers settle a broader policy covering isolated workspaces, custom binds, skill roots, and remote backends.

recommendation.title: Approve isolated writable none
recommendation.body: Implement the cross-backend fix so only the sandbox-owned workspace is writable for `none`, with live sandbox proof and regression coverage.
